1.title: Get the Mop!
1.topic: a tipped cup and a wet mess cleaned up at home (family, helping)
lines: *Tip*, | tip! | The *cup* | can *tip*!
*Drip*, | drop. | It is a *mess*. ↘
Can you *get* | the *mop*? ↗
*Yes*! | I can *get* it.
*Mop*, | mop, | *mop* | the *wet* spot.
Now it is *not* | a *mess*! ↘
sounds: 입을 크게 벌리고 짧게 '아'에 가까운 소리를 내요. '모프'가 아니라 '맙'처럼 짧게 끝내요.
입을 살짝만 벌리고 짧게 '이' 해요. '팁'을 길게 '티-입'으로 끌지 마요.
끝소리 p와 t는 '프', '트'를 붙이지 말고 입만 닫듯 짧게 멈춰요.
1.expression: Sound surprised on “Tip, tip!”, make a mopping motion on each “mop”, and finish with a proud smile.

2.title: Picture Day
2.topic: school picture day and wind-blown hair (school, feelings)
lines: On *picture day*, | Leo *brushed* his hair | very *neatly*.
On the way to school, | the *wind* *puffed* it up | like a *bird's nest*!
“Oh *no*!” | Leo *gasped*. ↘
He *pressed* it down | with both *hands*.
But it *popped* | right back *up*. ↘
“Say *cheese*!” | called the man | with the *camera*.
Leo *laughed* | and *forgot* | all about his hair.
It *turned out* | to be his *favorite* picture! ↘
sounds: sh, f, s, p 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t 소리예요. '브러쉬드'가 아니라 '브러쉬트'처럼 한 박자로 끝내요.
gh가 f 소리가 나요. laughed는 '래프트'처럼 한 박자로 읽어요.
ch는 입술을 앞으로 내밀고 '치', ee는 입꼬리를 옆으로 당겨 길게 '이-' 해요.
2.expression: Gasp with surprise on “Oh no!”, push down with your hands, and smile big on “Say cheese!”

3.title: Where Do Rainbows Come From?
3.topic: how sunlight and raindrops make a rainbow (science, weather)
lines: The rain *stops*. | The sun comes *out*. | And look— | a *rainbow*! ↘
But where do all those *colors* | come *from*? ↗
Sunlight looks *white*, | but it is really | a *mix* of many colors.
When sunlight shines | through *raindrops*, | the drops *bend* the light.
Then the colors *spread out* | like a *fan*.
Red is always on the *top*, | and *violet* is on the *bottom*.
In between are *orange*, | yellow, | green, | blue, | and *indigo*.
To see a rainbow, | the sun must be *behind* you | and the rain must be in *front* of you.
You can even *make* one | with a *garden hose* | on a sunny day!
Just stand with your *back* to the sun | and spray a fine *mist*. ↘
Science can be *beautiful*! ↘
sounds: 두 단어가 합쳐진 말은 앞 단어를 세게 읽어요: RAIN-bow (레인보우의 '레인'을 강하게).
v는 윗니를 아랫입술에 살짝 대고 목을 울려요. '바이올렛'처럼 b로 읽지 마요.
orange↗, yellow↗, green↗, blue↗, and indigo↘
여러 개를 나열할 때는 앞의 단어들은 살짝 올리고, 마지막 단어만 내려요.
3.expression: Start with wonder on “a rainbow!”, explain the middle like a science teacher, and end with a warm, amazed voice.

4.title: Jun's Gimbap Lunch
4.topic: a new student shares his Korean lunch and makes a friend (school, feelings, culture)
lines: On his *first* day at Maple School, | Jun held his lunch box | very *tightly*.
Inside were rolls of *gimbap* | that his *mom* had made | that morning.
At lunchtime, | a girl at his table | *pointed* at his food.
“What *is* that?” | she asked. ↗
Jun's cheeks turned *hot*. | He wanted to *hide* the box | under the table.
“It's... | *gimbap*,” | he said *quietly*. | “Rice and vegetables | rolled in *seaweed*.”
The girl's eyes went *wide*. | “*Seaweed*? | That's so *cool*!”
Her name was *Ava*, | and she had *never* tried it before.
Jun took a deep *breath* | and *offered* her a piece.
Ava *chewed* | and *nodded*. | “*Mmm*! | It's *salty* | and a little bit *sweet*!”
The next day, | Ava brought her grandma's *empanadas* | to share with Jun.
Soon, | their whole table was *sharing* bites | and telling *stories* | about their families' favorite foods.
Jun *still* held his lunch box | on the way to school— | but now he held it | *proudly*. ↘
sounds: 해설은 차분하게, 에이바의 질문은 궁금하게, 준은 처음엔 작고 수줍게, “That's so cool!”은 신나게 읽어요.
-ly는 약하고 짧게 '리'. 강세는 앞부분에 둬요. quietly는 세 박자 QUI-et-ly예요.
혀끝을 윗니 사이로 살짝 내밀어요. that은 '댓'이 아니고, breath 끝은 바람만 '스-' 나와요.
4.expression: Let your voice grow from nervous and quiet to warm and proud as Jun makes a new friend.
events: Jun held his lunch box tightly on his first day at a new school.
His mom had made gimbap for his lunch that morning.
A girl at his table pointed at his food and asked what it was.
Jun felt embarrassed and wanted to hide the box.
He quietly explained that gimbap is rice and vegetables rolled in seaweed.
Ava thought it was cool, and Jun offered her a piece.
The next day Ava brought her grandma's empanadas to share.
Soon the whole table shared food and stories, and Jun felt proud.
